title: The verifier's ballot admission: definitions, boards and pinned panels, with the rows 1.3, 2.3, 3.2, 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 and the report's ballots
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-ballots-vectors.py, from verifier-ceremony-vectors.py and ballot-vectors.py (independent Python implementations); membership proofs by packages/crypto/scripts/ballot-proofs.mjs, run outside the workspace with Semaphore 4.14.3's depth-32 circuit artifacts and snarkjs 0.7.5, whose groth16.verify gives every pairing verdict on the signals derived here from each record

cases.description: Seat 4 sends nothing, so seats 1 to 3 are registered. The board holds the transcript, then two admitted ballots, a ballot of each admission failure, a record that doesn't decode, a second admitted ballot by the first voter (a re-vote, not this part's to decide) and a byte-identical repeat of the first, which 5.7 rejects.
The same election with only admitted ballots after the transcript: 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 pass.

Copies of the first voter's ballot: one with another voter's proof (rejected, so it makes no copy a repeat, R4), then the original, a copy with its proof negated (other bytes, the same tier, nullifier and M), the second voter's ballot, a byte-identical copy and the first voter's re-vote (another M, so no repeat). 5.7 rejects the two copies after the original.
A copy of a ballot after a copy with another voter's proof, which is rejected: the admitted copy is no repeat (R4), so 5.7 passes.
The transcript and no ballot: 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 pass, with nothing admitted.
Two failures of 5.4 and one of 5.1 in another order: each row reports its own first failing entry.
Every seat registered: a share hash at seat 4 is admitted.
Seats 3 and 4 answer wrongly: no key set is registered, so no ballot is checked.
The definition names another membership key: 1.3 fails, and no ballot is checked under it.
A 2-of-4 panel where only seats 1 and 2 take part: the transcript registers a key set (k = 2) but 3.2 fails ceremony-participation, so no ballot is checked under it.
The profile pins ballot version 5, unknown here, with another membership key: 1.3 isn't failed, since a later release may pin that key for version 5, and 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 are unsupported.
The definition gives tier 2 a root of 0, which anyone can prove membership of (T-04): no ballot is checked under it.
The profile pins ballot version 2 under definition version 1, which no ballot context reads: 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 are unsupported.

Contract-event version 2 is pinned, so ballots arrive by the board path and the ordinary path (the board's BallotSubmitted), each copy judged by its own path (5.5): a board-path ballot; an ordinary one inside the window; ordinary ones a second before opening and after close; an ordinary copy of the first ballot at closes_at (inside, so a repeat); a board-path copy of the after-close ballot (it stands: a late copy never stands in for a timely one) and an ordinary copy of it at opens_at (inside, a repeat); an ordinary ballot naming another definition (5.1); the same log from an address the definition doesn't name, which carries no ballot; a board-path ballot in segment s_A = 169, the last allowed; and in segment 170 a copy of the first ballot and the early ballot, both boarded late, before any repeat.
A copy outside its window is rejected by 5.5 and so makes no later copy a repeat: the ordinary copy after it, at closes_at, stands.

The profile pins contract-event version 3, which 2.3 fails since the share-receipt batch (P1-12d), as it fails version 4 since the obligation root (P1-12f), but whose records the release still reads: a board-path ballot and its board-path copy, judged by 5.1 to 5.5, and the copy a repeat (5.7).

Contract-event version 3: the ballot relayed through L1 with a stamp after close, then an ordinary copy inside the window and a board-path copy. The relayed copy passes 5.1 to 5.4 and is set aside, since only 4.5's match with the relay's call proves its stamp: 5.5 and 5.7 are unverifiable (not-implemented) at it, whatever the other copies show, and the board-path copy stays a candidate repeat, since the relayed one may be the copy that stands.

The profile pins contract-event version 6, which this release doesn't read: the board-path ballot and its copy are judged by 5.1 to 5.4, but 5.5 and 5.7 are unsupported and the copy stays a candidate repeat.
